criteria.text: Every successful project save (not just the /restore path) appends exactly one project_revisions row.
The snapshot uses the freshly-incremented revision (revision_number = the RETURNING revision), so revision numbers are unique per project.
The snapshot row carries all required fields (snap_id uuid, project_id, revision_number, state, summary) so it can restore a previous version.
Revision numbers are unique per project at the DB level: a duplicate (project_id, revision_number) is rejected by a unique index.

Electron-mode (renderer/supabase-js) saves also snapshot history. Implemented server-side here (PostgresStorageBackend.save_project); the renderer path (277-C/D) needs a matching project_revisions insert in supabase-data.js sdSaveProject.
criteria.reason: Renderer-side snapshot belongs on the unmerged 277-C/D stack; this PR fixes the server-mode regression. Approach changed from a DB trigger to application-level because a trigger cannot run revisions.generate_summary (Python), cannot be deployed by the agent (gated), and removing the app-level snapshot before deploy would create a live-regression window. The unique-index migration (c4) ALSO needs a live supabase db push (human-authorized, like 277-B). See decisions.md 2026-06-06.
